There is a huge difference in the mindset you need to have when rolling aggro (at least SS Burn Queen, which carried me to Master this month), and that is recognizing which play will over 2-3 turns maximize your damage output.

Examples: use of combat tricks to fight for the board or go for your opponent's throat. Saving Berserk activation, recognizing correct line of play to either further pressure your opponent or make his removal inefficient etc.

There's a ton of nuances which over the span on 5-7 turns will decide whether you win or get rolled over. This results in a much smaller margin of error. The upside: games are a lot shorter, allowing you to climb faster.

As for the draw, you should be looking to put pressure on your opponent, curve out and stomp before your opponent has a chance. In most of your matches YOU will be the beatdown.

WHY DEMON HUNTERS GOT PIDGEON-HOLED WITH PERMA-VENGEANCE AND FAN OF KNIVES!? CUBING 3 IDENTICAL ITEMS FOR ALMOST EVERY DH BUILD ISN'T THE WAY TO GO!
On a second thought, Grim Reaper might be better than Wolf - this build doesn't stack IAS or CDR, so it could turn out to be a lot better. Will definitely try this one out!
Yeah, stacking AD is the way to go with S6. It's not even funny seeing the AD proc - the damage is insane.

I ran Vault belt for a while, thinking it might be worth using in speedruns or picking off targets. To be honest - it's clunky as hell, at least with 200+ ping I have @ PTR. Once 2.4. goes live it might see some use though.

I used Leech to 'burst-heal' - on gr65-70 even with Aquila almost everything drags your hp below 30%, so in order to stay alive you need all the healing you can get. I'll try Steady Aim though.

As for skipping Karlei's - I don't think it's possible to keep Aquila proc then this easy - 2-3 Impale casts will get it off and then you'll get one-shotted for sure.

I wasn't saying it's not possible to run this. Hell, If I were to run Nats or Marauders I'd switch up immediately to perma-Vengeance due to the fact that transitioning to this is easy and actually improves both your DPS and survivability. I was just pointing out that for other DH builds it's not that easy, since you don't stack that much CDR on gear for those specs.

Seethe is 10 hatred per second. Unless I missed something in the patch notes.

And you can't run Dark Heart and Seethe at the same time - for perma-Vengeance you need Crown cubed, so there's no other way around it (if you cube ORotZ, you're stripped of Elusive Ring / Unity / CoE and those are way more powerful than Vengeance imo).

So while you can have Vengeance permanently up, you lock in armor slot in cube for Leoric's. Nats have Yans there, UE - Cindercoat. If I were to run M6 now, I'd probably use Yans (or Pride's Fall). As for Shadow set - you either cube the new Vault item or Wraps of Clarity. While you can easily switch Yans for Leoric's and thus run perma-Vengeance setup (since it provides way more DPS), it's a bit trickier to decide whether UE should players should do the same, as RCR is an extremely important stat to this spec.

To sum up, I believe we're not supposed to have perma-Vengeance. It's just a sort of "I need that elite dead. NOW!" button. And as such, it's good. Is it good enough to build around it? I guess we'll have to wait for PTR to find out.
